newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Bratislava bourse edges up on stronger VSZ shares.
newsitem.headline: Bratislava bourse edges up on stronger VSZ shares.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange's SAX index firmed 0.6 points to 207.39 in thinner trading on Friday, pushed higher by gains to the average price of VSZ shares.
VSZ closed unchanged at 750 crowns, but its average price -- which is used for calculating the index -- rose 1.1 percent.

"Investors are willing to accept this year's high of VSZ shares, 750 crowns, but there are not enough shares on offer to meet demand," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings. "(But) demand is not strong enough to push it further at any cost."

Most blue chips traded very low volumes and Sykora said liquidity problems could be solved by issuance of new shares. But he pointed out that Slovak firms very seldom turn to capital market to obtain funds for their investment programmes.
"Majority owners do not want to lose their positions, and, on the other hand, they appear not to have enough funds to subscribe to sufficient amounts of potential new share issues," he said.
Overall volume rose to 220,449 shares -- boosted mainly through direct -- from 178,703 shares, while turnover increased to 107.35 million crowns from 80.72 million on Thursday.
